string.name: troubleshoot_discovery_desc
troubleshoot_discovery_service_hint
string.value:
LocalSend on iOS/Android sometimes appears open but its service has not actually started.
If devices cannot be discovered, clear it from the background and reopen the app.

string.name: troubleshoot_slow_transfer_desc
string.value:
Start with three simple checks:
1. Make sure both devices are connected to the same 5GHz Wi-Fi; do not leave one on 5GHz and the other on 2.4GHz (2.4GHz is much slower).
2. Check the Wi-Fi connection speed: Settings > WLAN > tap the connected network > Connection speed. If it is below 300Mbps, move closer to the router or make sure you are on 5GHz. If it shows 800Mbps or more but transfers are still slow, the limit is usually router forwarding or the other device.
3. Use a broadband speed test only as a reference: the test also uses the device-to-router Wi-Fi link. If the broadband test is normal (for example, a 300M connection reaches 30–40MB/s) but local transfers are clearly slower, the bottleneck is local forwarding or the other device. If the broadband test is also low, move closer to the router and test again to rule out Wi-Fi signal/band issues; if it is still low after moving closer, the broadband speed is low, but broadband does not participate in local transfers and is unrelated to this issue.

Common causes:
- When both devices are on the same 5GHz router, data goes through the router twice (receive and retransmit), so the actual speed is usually about half of a single device's test. When both devices transfer through the same router's Wi-Fi, mid-range and entry-level home routers usually cannot sustain more than 50MB/s.
- Long distance, walls, weak signal, or many nearby Wi-Fi networks can all reduce speed.
- Many small files are slower than one large file; this is normal.
- If a computer is connected by Ethernet, a 100Mbps port or cable has a theoretical limit of about 12.5MB/s.

string.name: troubleshoot_slow_transfer_highlight
string.value:
The most effective fix:
Enable the hotspot directly on the HarmonyOS device (a HarmonyOS device can usually keep Wi-Fi and the hotspot enabled at the same time) and let the other device connect to that hotspot; transfer speeds can often exceed 100MB/s.

string.name: troubleshoot_connection_desc
string.value:
Check whether the target device is running and the IP address is correct.
Make sure no VPN is interfering with local network access.

string.name: troubleshoot_protocol_desc
string.value:
Both devices must have compatible encryption settings to communicate.
If one uses HTTPS and the other uses HTTP, they cannot discover or connect to each other.
Make sure the encryption settings match on both sides (Settings > LocalSend > Advanced settings > Encrypted transfer).

string.name: troubleshoot_multi_interface_desc
string.value:
Having multiple network interfaces enabled simultaneously (e.g., Ethernet + Wi-Fi or dual Wi-Fi) may cause device discovery issues: broadcasts may go through the wrong interface.
Disable unnecessary interfaces or select the correct one in Settings > LocalSend > Advanced settings > Network interface.

string.name: troubleshoot_transfer_interrupt_desc
troubleshoot_remote_desc
string.value:
HandySend works within the same local network by default.
For cross-network transfers, use a virtual networking tool (e.g., EasyTier) to create a virtual LAN:
1. Enable the corresponding network interface in Settings > LocalSend > Advanced settings > Network interface;
2. For web transfer, also allow that interface in Settings > Web Transfer > Advanced settings > Network interface and select the matching address.

string.name: troubleshoot_duplicate_desc
string.value:
[LocalSend]
If the other party resets their security certificate (device fingerprint), the same device will appear with a different identity, causing duplicates in the list.
Tap the refresh button to refresh the device list and resolve this.

[MTA]
MTA devices are distinguished by their Bluetooth identifier; duplicates may briefly appear if the peer's Bluetooth identifier changes, and devices that stop advertising are removed automatically.
You can also tap the refresh button to rescan and clear duplicates immediately.

string.name: troubleshoot_mta_transfer_desc
troubleshoot_mta_transfer_hint
string.value:
The "Detailed logging (DEBUG)" switch turns off automatically after the app restarts.
Reproduce the problem right after enabling it and do not restart the app in the meantime.

string.name: troubleshoot_offline_title
string.value: Why Do Offline Devices Still Appear in the List

string.name: troubleshoot_offline_desc
string.value:
Offline devices do not disappear from Nearby Devices immediately.
- A LAN (LocalSend) device is removed after a refresh confirmation once it stops announcing;
- An MTA (Mutual Transfer Alliance) device relies on BLE advertisements for its online status and is removed automatically after about 30 seconds without any advertisement, reappearing in real time once it comes back online.
To save power, MTA discovery scanning only runs while the Send page is visible.

string.name: troubleshoot_web_usage_desc
troubleshoot_web_unreachable_title
string.value: Web Address Does Not Open or Access Code Is Invalid

string.name: troubleshoot_web_unreachable_desc
troubleshoot_web_encryption_title
string.value: Why Is Web Transfer Unencrypted by Default

string.name: troubleshoot_web_encryption_desc
string.value:
Encrypted web transfer is off by default and is independent of the LocalSend encryption setting.
To enable it, go to Settings > Web Transfer > Advanced settings > Encrypted transfer.
It uses a self-signed certificate, which browsers or ad-blocking extensions may block.
If downloads fail, temporarily disable encryption or turn off the extension and retry.

string.name: troubleshoot_web_background_title
string.value: Web Page Is Unreachable After Switching to the Background

string.name: troubleshoot_web_background_desc
string.value:
The web service runs as long as the app does.
With "Allow background receiving" enabled in Settings > General, the app stays in the background for about 5 minutes when no transfer is running, and the web page remains reachable during that time.
After it times out, or after web transfer is stopped manually, the page cannot be opened; keep the app in the foreground for long sharing sessions.
